stem: Manganese, chromium and ruthenium are all transition elements.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Explain what is meant by a *transition element*.

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: $\text{MnO}_4^-\text{(aq)}$ and $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\text{(aq)}$ act as oxidising agents in acidic solution. Both these oxidising agents will oxidise a solution of $\text{Sn}^{2+}$ to give a solution of $\text{Sn}^{4+}$. Solutions containing $\text{Sn}^{2+}$ and solutions containing $\text{Sn}^{4+}$ are colourless.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.text:
Describe the colour change seen when an excess of $\text{Sn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ is added separately to

- dilute acidified $\text{MnO}_4^-\text{(aq)}$

- dilute acidified $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: Write an equation for the reaction between $\text{Sn}^{2+}\text{(aq)}$ and acidified $\text{Cr}_2\text{O}_7^{2-}\text{(aq)}$.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
Ruthenium, Ru, forms complex ions. In one such complex ion, **X**, the ruthenium ion has a co-ordination number of six. Each complex ion **X** contains one $\text{Ru}^{2+}$ ion, one $\text{Cl}^-$ ion, one $\text{SO}_2$ molecule and the remaining ligands are $\text{NH}_3$ molecules.

The $\text{SO}_2$ molecule acts as a monodentate ligand and is attached to the $\text{Ru}^{2+}$ ion via the sulfur atom. **X** exists in two isomeric forms.

parts.label: (c)(i)
parts.text: State what is meant by a *co-ordination number of six*.

parts.label: (c)(ii)
parts.text: State the formula of **X**. Include its charge.

parts.label: (c)(iii)
parts.text:
Draw the two isomeric forms of **X** in the boxes below. Your diagrams should show

- the three-dimensional shapes of the two isomers
- how each ligand is attached to the central ruthenium ion.

{{figure:pdf_visual_01.png}}

parts.label: (c)(iv)
parts.text: Suggest the type of isomerism shown by **X**.

parts.label: (c)(v)
parts.text: Explain the origin of colour in a transition element complex such as **X**.
